text: #857's ratified plan, step 2 of #789, recorded at its merge as the plan asks. What a bug's statement says of the code is part of what a person ratifies. A bug statement may carry code_behavior: current when the code has the bug today, as the issue, unchanged code or tests report, and hypothetical when nothing says it does. The field enters the proposal hash with the rest of the statement, so adding, changing or removing it is an amendment that needs its own ratification, and the scope and ratification checks refuse a lock that differs by it from the proposal a person ratified. A lock from before the field keeps its exact JSON and its hash: nothing infers a classification for it or migrates it, and its bugs read not replayed: not classified. Every bug in a new modeled proposal or preview is classified. A gate from before the field reads a classified lock without it, computes another proposal hash and fails its ratification check, so a repository moves the gate it pins before its factory drafts with this rule. It's a one-way door because every lock ratified with a classification from here on rests on how the field is hashed.
